tender.title: BARRIER QUALIFICATION CHAMBER - UNIVERSITY OF ABERDEEN
tender.description:
Award of contract
The National Decommissioning Centre at the University of Aberdeen has identified the need for a downhole testing facility with the primary purpose of evaluating the behaviour of new materials for plugging and abandonment (P&A) of oil and gas wells. Existing and emerging alternative plugging technologies require a framework for validation and qualification.  A test facility is to be built for this purpose.
The facility will have to mimic downhole conditions such as pressure and temperature and allow a test tool to be deployed and activated before enabling a pressure test of the seal.

tender.description:
Hampshire County Council (HCC) is seeking to replace its existing Place, Connectivity & Infrastructure Professional Services Framework (ET14110) by establishing a new four-year multi-supplier Framework for the provision of specialist technical transportation and civil engineering professional services, together with infrastructure development and support services. The Framework aims to provide HCC with continued engineering infrastructure and development consultancy services and allows for provision for specialist technical transportation and engineering services.
The Framework includes but is not limited to the following technical professional services:
Lot A - Multi-Disciplinary Services
• Sustainable and accessible transport infrastructure planning services
• Highways, Transportation, Civil and Structural engineering design services
• Design and advice services under Section 278 and 38 of the Highways Act (1980) 
• Construction estimating, commercial and financial management services 
• Safety audit, engineering and management
• Waste infrastructure and development design services
• Flood and water management and drainage design services
• Ecological and environmental services
• Landscape architecture and design services
• Sustainable and community integration strategic planning
• Infrastructure technology strategy and design services
• Intelligent traffic systems design and advice services
• Building Information Modelling (BIM) services
B1 - Engineering Design Specialisms
• Bridge and Structural inspections including masonry, reinforced concrete, post tensioned and steel structures
• Infrastructure design services covering developments, minor and specialist street and transportation design services 
• Inclusive and Public Realm Design, including transport design services
• 3D and BIM modelling and Visualisations and animations (for engagement purposes)
• Flood and water management services including hydraulic modelling
• LLFAs support and design services
• Highways drainage design services including SuDs
• Development drainage assessment services and design checking services
• Design of small scale waste water treatment plants
B2 - Transport Planning Specialisms
• Active Travel and healthy streets, including walking and cycling design specialisms, Pedestrian wayfinding signage strategies and Urban area cycle network strategies
• Accessible infrastructure and planning services including inclusive design, low traffic neighbourhoods and school streets
• Future mobility planning services (including local mobility hubs, e-mobility solutions, electric vehicle charging etc.) and Low carbon approaches
• Travel Data and Modelling including Walking and cycling data, Travel and journey modelling, Car parking data, Intelligent traffic data (including queue surveys), TAG Compliant traffic modelling and Real time journey information visualisations, business engagement
• Planning including school travel planning, local travel plans and support
• Business case development and Scheme economic appraisal including Cost Benefit Analysis services, Sustainability appraisals
• Bid application preparations including DfT Full Business Case services, Specialist business case and funding bid support
• Master planning services including Land use / spatial planning services
• Associated general research services
B3 - Strategic Planning Specialism
• Planning application support services
• Planning appeals support services
• Town & Country planning Act support services
• Strategic & spatial planning services
• Developer and stakeholder engagement services
B4 - Environmental, Sustainability and Decarbonisation Specialisms
• Air quality zone modelling & assessment
• Air quality, health and environmental research services (in the context of transport)
• Modelling and advice services
• Action plan support services (in the context of transport)
• Vehicle emission modelling / simulation services
• Sustainable travel and transport consultancy services & decarbonisation, including Carbon offsetting advice
• Health impact surveys and assessments including noise monitoring
• Waste management planning
• Environmental audits and Socio-economic appraisals
• Environmental survey, inspection and supervision services including Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA)
B5 - Ecological, Landscape & Arboriculture Specialisms
• Landscape design & management services
• Arboriculture planting & management advice
• Arboriculture surveys & assessments including TPO & felling advice
• Arboriculture and landscape survey, inspection and supervision services
• Ecological & habitat assessments and surveys
• Ecological appraisals and Ecological Impact Assessments
• Protected species surveys & assessment, for animals including but not limited to otters, bats, dormice, etc., or for birds
• Ecological survey, inspection and supervision services
B6 - Advice and Community Engagement for Active Travel Specialism
• Community engagement services for sustainable travel, such as surveys, school streets, community events
• Applying behavioural change science for sustainable travel solutions
• School engagement services for active travel including cycling and walking
B7 - Traffic Management, Traffic Order and Parking Consultancy
• Traffic Orders - drafting, consolidation, TRO reviews, variations and amendments
• Digital TRO mapping – Interface with Traffic Order management software
• Signs and lining reviews – including Parking, Speed Limits, Movement Restrictions
• Parking reviews including On-road and Off-road parking and resident parking schemes
• Moving Traffic Enforcement – development and delivery of schemes.
• Low cost Traffic Management measures
B8 - Street Lighting Design Specialism
• Scoping/feasibility of street lighting projects
• Preliminary and detailed design of lighting schemes, including drawings and schedules, to British and EU standards 
• Lighting designs to meet planning consent/conditions, including minimising impact on local ecology 
• S278 and S38 street lighting designs with accompanying PFI Certificate of Approval
• Support PFI Street Lighting accrual process
The new Framework will be divided into nine separate lots. Lot A will deliver larger scale multi-disciplinary consultancy services and Lot B will be sub dividend into eight smaller-scale specialist consultancy services.
The Framework will be available to all Public Bodies within the geographical area of England (e.g. Local Authorities, NHS, Fire, Police, schools etc.), but predominantly those within the South East and South West regions. These public bodies shall be named as ‘Participating Authorities’ for the purposes of this Framework but Hampshire County Council shall remain the named lead ‘Contracting Authority’ for the purposes of this procurement and will retain overall control and ownership of the Framework. This Framework will be an NEC4 Framework Contract, with call-offs through the Framework using the NEC4 Professional Service Contract (PSC) and Professional Service Short Contract (PSSC).

• Tenderers shall only be permitted to tender for either Lot A or Lot B, tenderers cannot bid for both. Those Tenderers applying to Lot B, can tender for 1 or more of the specialisms.  
• Lot A ‘Multi-disciplinary Services’ shall comprise a maximum of 3 large multi-disciplinary engineering professional services companies, for the provision of engineering services.

tender.title: School Leadership Development
tender.description:
The North East MSA seeks to appoint a partner to design and deliver a leadership programme to support a minimum of 110 school leaders from across Northumberland, Newcastle, North Tyneside, County Durham, Gateshead, South Tyneside and Sunderland. This will include a dedicated approach to leadership development and additional support specially designed to meet local priorities and provide networking and best practice sharing opportunities.
The work we intend to commission will support the professional development of school leaders across the North East, including the provision of access to the latest education research, and high-quality methodologies to facilitate the sharing of best practice. This service should be distinct from, and not duplicate, existing provision e.g. National Professional Qualifications. This proposed work should therefore include activities that meet Priority 3 within the Excellence in Education Programme, which focus on improving teacher wellbeing, professional development and teacher retention.
Delivery partners will be expected to: 
•	Deliver a strategic approach to leadership development across a range of key competencies.
•	Provide professional development for school leadership staff in primary schools.
•	Provide professional development for middle leadership staff in primary schools.
•	Provide professional development for early years leaders.
•	Provide professional development for SENDCos
•	Provide opportunities for leaders to engage in communities of research and best practice.
•	Provide ongoing 1:1 support for each participating leader.
•	Have capacity to deliver to a minimum of 110 school leaders across the North East over a one-year period.
•	Provide an in-person introductory session to bring together leaders from participating schools to launch the initiative, and subsequent additional in-person events.
•	Provide an impact study to evaluate the effectiveness of the programme.
•	Participate in North East MSA's ongoing evaluation of the Excellence in Education programme as required.

tender.title: Innovation Marketplace
tender.description:
The Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (DBIST) and the Government Commercial Agency (GCA) are working together to establish an Innovation Marketplace, providing a compliant route for public sector buyers to identify and procure innovative products, services and solutions that address operational, service delivery and policy challenges.
This requirement supports wider government work to improve how innovation is identified, tested and scaled, while reducing barriers for innovative suppliers, including SMEs, start-ups and scale-ups, to access public sector opportunities.
The scope is expected to include establishing and operating a Dynamic Market for innovation, enabling eligible suppliers to apply to join throughout the life of the arrangement. The Innovation Marketplace may cover a broad range of innovative technologies, products, services and solutions that support public sector transformation, improved outcomes, efficiency, and economic growth.
The Innovation Marketplace is intended to be used by central government departments, arm’s length bodies and other eligible public sector organisations. It is expected to support procurement following pre-market engagement, challenge definition, pilots, proofs of concept or other evidence-building activity.
The arrangement is expected to complement the Innovation Hub (Commercial Innovation Hub - Find a Tender) by providing a transparent, fair and compliant commercial route for buyers to procure relevant innovative solutions.
Our ambition is to make the government a more strategic buyer of innovation. The result is a more connected innovation ecosystem where innovative suppliers can scale more quickly, government can access better solutions faster, and public money works harder to support both public service transformation and economic growth.
When contacting GCA regarding this agreement, please ensure that you reference the agreement details in all correspondence.

Lot 1 - Perinatal Mental Health Peer Support Service Lot 2 - Perinatal Mental Health - Dads and Male Caregivers Peer Support Lot 1 - Perinatal Mental Health Peer Support Service Sheffield City Council, as part of the national Best Start in Life and Healthy Babies Programme (formerly Start for Life), is recommissioning a perinatal mental health peer support service to provide early, accessible, and relationship based support for parents experiencing mild to moderate mental health difficulties [1]. This includes anxiety, low mood, stress, and supporting healthy parent–infant relationships. The need for strengthened peer based emotional wellbeing support has been consistently highlighted by parents and carers, including through the Sheffield Early Years consultation (2023) and subsequent engagement activity undertaken more recently. This has been running for 3 years and the aim is to build on, develop, improve and evolve what has already been implemented. Lot 2 - Perinatal Mental Health - Dads and Male Caregivers Peer Support Sheffield City Council, as part of the national Best Start in Life and Healthy Babies Programme (formerly Start for Life), is recommissioning a Perinatal Mental Health (PNMH) Peer Support Programme for Dads and Male Caregivers. This recommissioning builds on three years of delivery and responds directly to needs identified through the 2023 Early Years Start for Life Consultation, where fathers and partners highlighted gaps in support during the perinatal period. The aim of this programme is to help all new and expectant dads and male caregivers make the transition to parenthood as smooth as possible, with a strong emphasis on: • sensitive and attuned caregiving • positive early parent–infant relationships • good mental wellbeing for babies and their families

tender.title: Leadership Development Programme to Reduce Lost Learning
tender.description:
Children in the North East face significantly poorer educational outcomes simply because of where they grow up. In summer 2025, the North East had a 4% drop in the proportion of young people achieve A and A* grades which significantly impacts their future opportunities. It is the only region in England where these top grades have not surpassed pre-pandemic levels. Pupils are also less likely to achieve top GCSE grades: 17.8%, compared to 28.4% achieved in London. 
These grades are crucial to young people applying to competitive universities or apprenticeship places.
Schools in our region are severely impacted by absence, exclusions and SEND. Last year, schools in the North East had the highest absence rate in England, with almost one in five pupils in the region severely absent (missing over 10% of classes). The region also has nearly a third of pupils eligible for free school meals (compared to a quarter nationally) and the highest rate of pupils with SEND in the country. Child poverty underlies many of these issues, with an excellent education the best hope for our young people to break the cycle. 
This proposal aims to provide a means for schools to take a more relational approach to children experiencing challenges in attending school, resulting in a reduction of unnecessary exclusions and fixed-term suspensions. Thus, helping the EiE Programme to meet its desired outcome of improving attendance levels in North East schools.
The appointed provider will design and deliver a model for school leaders which develops practice and expertise to implement a whole-school approach to inclusion. The approach may include, but is not limited to:
•	School leader workshops
•	Provision of strategic tools to support implementation
•	Share national best practice
•	Use technology where appropriate

Norfolk County Council (NCC) proposes to procure an Occupational Therapy, Inclusion and Participation Service, which will form part of Norfolk's zone based, multidisciplinary Experts at Hand model.  
'Experts at Hand' is designed to transform how support for children and young people with SEND is delivered, by bringing specialist expertise directly into mainstream early years, primary, secondary and post-16 settings. By embedding 'expert roles',
such as occupational therapists alongside setting staff, and wider professionals. The offer supports earlier identification of need, strengthens workforce confidence and capability, and provides timely, evidence-based support within everyday learning environments.
The Experts at Hand offer will support mainstream settings across early years, primary, secondary and post-16, to better identify and meet the needs of children and young people with emerging or identified SEND needs. It will provide dedicated professional expertise tailored to the needs of individual children and young people, through observation, assessment, and identifying appropriated targeted support to help more children and young people flourish within their settings.
The contract is anticipated to start 4th January 2027 up to 31st March 2029 with an anticipated contract value of £3,383,930 excluding VAT.

tender.title: Reading Fluency Peer Tutoring
tender.description:
We propose to extend the North East MSA's current Fast Forward to reading Fluency project into the next Academic Year (2026/27), building upon the success of the current cohort, but narrowing the focus to 20 of our schools that will benefit the most from this approach. 
Over the past year, work has demonstrated that targeted investment in reading fluency can deliver measurable gains for pupils across the North East. 
Hundreds of pupils have become more confident, fluent readers, with consistent improvements across standardised assessments. These outcomes matter, not only for attainment, but for pupils' ability to access the full curriculum and improve their life chances.  
The delivery partner will be expected to design and deliver a peer mediated reading aloud intervention providing:
•	20 minute in-school sessions, twice weekly 
•	Carefully sequenced anthologies designed to develop reading fluency, vocabulary and background knowledge 
•	Texts spanning a wide range of curriculum rich domains, including history, geography, science and the arts, supporting both literacy and wider knowledge building 
•	A structured approach to improving reading 
•	Delivery through trained peer tutors, typically Year 10 or Year 12 pupils 
Schools should be supported to review existing attainment data, and the delivery partner should undertake diagnostic assessment to identify pupils most in need. 
Each participating school will identify 20 pupils, randomly assigned to: 
•	Intervention group, n equals 10, who receive FFA immediately 
•	Control group, n equals 10, who receive FFA following the trial period 
The Delivery Partner should have capacity to deliver to up to 20 schools across the North East MSA footprint, and:
•	Provide an impact study to evaluate the effectiveness of the programme.
•	Provide an in person introductory session to bring together representatives of participating schools to launch the initiative, and subsequent additional network events.

NHS Thames Valley (TV) Integrated Care Board (ICB), (the Commissioner) is seeking suitable providers who have the capability and capacity to deliver Complex Termination of Pregnancy (CTOP) service, in line with the specified requirements, in the capacity of the Regional Network Lead Provider (Hub) responsible for the delivery, coordination and clinical governance of CTOP pathways across the South East region. For the remainder of this document this will be referred to as the: Complex Termination of Pregnancy (CTOP) service.
The Hub will deliver specialist medical and surgical termination of pregnancy care up to 23 + 6 weeks' gestation. The Hub will also host the regional Single Point of Access (SPOA) and Multidisciplinary Team (MDT), lead on regional training and governance across providers. (NHS and Independent Sector Providers (ISP) where there are interdependencies/interfaces with NHS services). Alongside the coordination of the network of NHS providers across the South East to ensure equitable, safe, and high-quality CTOP care.
The service specification can be found at https://www.england.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/1834-Service-Specification-final.pdf 
Please also see the CTOP Service Model document hosted within the e-procurement system (Atamis) for a full description of the anticipated CTOP service across the South East.
The procurement will establish one Regional Lead Centre (Hub) responsible for:
•	Hosting the Single Point of Access (SPOA) for all CTOP referrals in the South East.
•	Leading the Regional Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) to review, triage, and allocate cases across the network.
•	Delivering direct clinical care for patients requiring both medical and surgical terminations up to 23 + 6 weeks' gestation.
•	Providing clinical governance and quality oversight for all Network Member Providers (Spokes).
•	Leading the training, upskilling, and maintenance-of-skills programme for the regional CTOP workforce, in line with the national CTOP service specification.
•	Coordinating regional data collection, audit, outcome reporting, and shared learning to ensure consistent standards of care across the South East.
Background:
The national Complex Termination of Pregnancy (CTOP) service was established following publication of the NHS England Service Specification (2021) to ensure that patients with significant co-morbidities or medical complications requiring termination of pregnancy receive care in appropriately equipped NHS hospitals with access to multidisciplinary teams, diagnostics, surgical facilities, critical care, and blood transfusion services.
Currently, provision within the South East is variable. While several NHS Trusts provide elements of the service, there is no formally commissioned or coordinated regional network. The absence of a lead centre and a standardised referral pathway has resulted in patients travelling long distances to receive care in other regions, and in inconsistent access to clinical expertise, workforce resilience, and quality oversight.
This procurement seeks to address those inequities by establishing a Regional CTOP Hub-and-Network model, ensuring that every patient in the South East region can access safe, timely, and locally coordinated care.
Service Model Overview
The Regional Lead Provider (Hub) will:
•	Operate as the central coordination point for all CTOP referrals via a Single Point of Access (SPOA).
•	Host the regional CTOP MDT, bringing together consultants in obstetrics, gynaecology, anaesthesia, fetal medicine, maternal medicine, nursing/midwifery, radiology, pathology, and bereavement support to agree appropriate care pathways for each case.
•	Deliver both medical and surgical CTOP procedures up to 23 + 6 weeks' gestation for eligible patients.
•	Support Network Member Providers in delivering CTOP services within lower gestational limits (e.g. up to 13 + 6 or 19 + 6 weeks), providing clinical advice, escalation pathways, and governance oversight.
•	Provide clinical and operational leadership for the South East CTOP Network, ensuring alignment with national standards and the NHS England CTOP specification.
•	Lead the regional training programme to build and sustain CTOP workforce capability across the network.
•	Undertake regional data collection, analysis, and submission to NHS England, including audit of outcomes, equity of access, and quality indicators.
The network model will be designed to ensure consistent governance, integrated clinical pathways, and robust quality assurance. The Hub will be responsible for convening network meetings, facilitating shared learning, maintaining the risk register, and reporting performance and compliance to commissioners.
Scope of Services:
The procured service will include, but not be limited to:
•	Provision of specialist medical and surgical termination of pregnancy services up to 23 + 6 weeks.
•	Access to on-site or formalised arrangements for theatres, diagnostics, blood products, critical care, and other relevant specialities.
•	Delivery of pre-, peri-, and post-procedure care, including counselling, anaesthetic support, and bereavement care.
•	Implementation of robust clinical governance and audit processes across the network.
•	Participation in national reporting and assurance processes, including the Abortion Notification System and NHS Maternity Services Dataset.
•	Leadership of regional training and competency maintenance, in line with the national CTOP service specification.
•	Ensuring compliance with all relevant legislation, including the Abortion Act 1967, Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014, Equality Act 2010, and NHS England's Health Inequalities Improvement Framework.
Expected Outcomes:
The procurement will ensure:
•	Equitable access to complex termination services across all South East ICB areas.
•	Reduction in patient travel outside of region for late-gestation or complex procedures.
•	Consistent standards of clinical governance and safety across all providers.
•	Development of a sustainable regional workforce with maintained surgical and medical CTOP skills.

The provider must be registered with the Care Quality Commission (CQC) to deliver Termination of Pregnancy (ToP) services under the regulated activity "Termination of pregnancies," as set out in the Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014.
Providers must demonstrate and maintain full compliance with CQC fundamental standards, including those relating to safety, effectiveness, leadership, and quality of care.
Evidence of current CQC registration, scope of registration, and latest compliance status must be provided as part of the submission.
2.	Professional Registration and Competence
All clinicians delivering the Complex Termination of Pregnancy (CTOP) service must hold appropriate registration with the relevant professional body, and must be in good standing with their regulator.
This includes, but is not limited to:
Medical practitioners: registration with the General Medical Council (GMC) and possession of a valid licence to practise.
Nursing and midwifery staff: registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC).
Anaesthetists, radiologists, sonographers, and pathology specialists: registration with the relevant professional council (e.g. GMC, HCPC, or Royal College).
All clinical staff must work within their professional scope of practice, maintain continuing professional development (CPD) in accordance with their regulator's requirements, and engage in annual appraisal and revalidation.
The provider must ensure that competency frameworks, supervision, and peer review are embedded within governance structures.
3.	Abortion Act 1967 Compliance
All practitioners undertaking terminations must comply with the Abortion Act 1967 (as amended) and associated Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) regulations.
Key legal requirements include:
Certification by two registered medical practitioners confirming that statutory grounds for termination are met.
Accurate and timely notification of all procedures to the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) in accordance with DHSC reporting requirements.
Compliance with national guidance on consent, safeguarding, confidentiality, and record keeping.
The provider must have robust governance arrangements in place to ensure all statutory obligations under the Abortion Act are fulfilled.
4.	Governance and Clinical Leadership
The provider must designate a named Clinical Lead for the CTOP service who:
Is a consultant-level clinician with demonstrable experience in complex pregnancy management.
Provides clinical leadership and oversight of service quality, safety, and outcomes.
Chairs multidisciplinary team (MDT) discussions and morbidity and mortality (M&M) reviews.
Ensures compliance with national service specifications, NICE guidance, and NHS England governance frameworks.
The provider's clinical governance structure must define clear lines of accountability to the Board and align with NHS England's quality and safety assurance requirements.
5.	Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) and Supporting Specialists
The provider must demonstrate access to a comprehensive MDT with relevant expertise to deliver holistic, safe, and compassionate care for women and birthing people requiring complex termination.
The MDT should include (but not be limited to):
Fetal Medicine
Obstetrics
Anaesthetics
Nursing and Midwifery (including Specialist Bereavement Support)
Psychology or Counselling
Pathology
Safeguarding / Social Care Liaison
All MDT members must meet relevant professional registration and revalidation standards, and participate in regular audit, clinical review, and shared learning.
6.	Corporate and Trade Standing
The provider must be a legally constituted organisation authorised to deliver healthcare services within England and capable of entering into NHS contracts.
Requirements include:
Registration as an NHS Trust, Foundation Trust, or other recognised healthcare provider entity.
Financial and organisational stability, with evidence of appropriate insurance and indemnity.
Compliance with procurement and contracting frameworks, including enrolment on NHS Provider Frameworks, Contracts Finder, or Find a Tender platforms as applicable.
Assurance that all directors and senior officers meet the "fit and proper persons" requirement under Regulation 5 of the Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014.
The provider must maintain effective governance, safeguarding, and information governance frameworks in line with NHS England and statutory requirements.
7.	Ongoing Assurance and Monitoring
The provider must be able to demonstrate systems and processes that ensure continued compliance with:
CQC registration conditions and notifications.
Professional revalidation and appraisal cycles.
Abortion Act reporting obligations.
Annual audit and peer review outcomes.
Learning and improvement mechanisms following incidents, patient feedback, or regulatory inspection.
Regular monitoring of compliance will form part of the ongoing contract management and quality assurance processes between NHS England and the provider.

tender.title: Heritage Consultant - Lymington Sea Water Baths
tender.description:
Lymington and Pennington Town Council is seeking to appoint one suitably experienced Heritage Consultant to undertake a comprehensive heritage review of the Lymington Sea Water Baths as part of a National Lottery Heritage Fund supported feasibility and development project.
The Lymington Sea Water Baths were established in 1833 and are among the earliest surviving open-air seawater bathing facilities in the United Kingdom. The site has significant architectural, cultural and social heritage value, but is at risk because of structural deterioration, historic alterations and continued exposure to the marine environment.
The consultant will provide an authoritative assessment of the historical development, architectural features, surviving fabric, cultural value and heritage significance of the site. The work will inform architectural and engineering design up to RIBA Stage 2, community engagement, interpretation planning, conservation decision making and the evidence base for future capital funding applications.
The commission will include:
• Reviewing existing reports, historic surveys, photographs, maps, newspapers, trade directories, archives and local records.
• Undertaking archival and documentary research, including engagement with relevant local museums, archives, historians and heritage organisations.
• Establishing a detailed chronology of the development and use of the Baths, including their earlier origins, subsequent alterations and changing role within the community.
• Assessing the heritage significance of the pool layout, historic engineering, aeration fountains, concrete structures, buildings, setting, views and surviving architectural features.
• Assessing the social and cultural history of the Baths, including their contribution to leisure, health, wellbeing, tourism and local identity.
• Identifying heritage sensitivities, constraints, risks and opportunities that should inform the design process.
• Advising the appointed architectural and engineering team during the development of proposals up to RIBA Stage 2.
• Preparing conservation principles and heritage guidance to support future decisions concerning repair, alteration, restoration and development.
• Working collaboratively with the Council, Project Manager, Design Team, Quantity Surveyor, Consultation and Engagement Consultant and other appointed specialists.
• Providing accessible heritage stories, themes and supporting content for public consultation, exhibitions and future interpretation.
• Supporting the integration of heritage considerations into community engagement and design development.
The required deliverables are expected to include:
A heritage scoping note and initial issues log.
A detailed Heritage Review Report, provided in draft and final form.
A Heritage Significance Assessment prepared using an appropriate recognised conservation methodology.
Heritage advice and design integration notes for the RIBA Stage 0 to 2 design process.
Guidance identifying heritage constraints, sensitivities and opportunities.
Interpretation themes, stories and accessible heritage content for use in engagement activities and future interpretation.
A concise summary suitable for inclusion in National Lottery Heritage Fund reporting, evaluation and future funding submissions.
All reports and supporting materials must be clearly written, accessible, appropriately illustrated and suitable for use by the Council, its professional advisers, community stakeholders and the National Lottery Heritage Fund. Research sources and supporting evidence must be clearly referenced.
The consultant will be expected to attend project meetings and workshops as reasonably required, provide timely advice during design development and coordinate their work with the wider project programme.
The contract is for one Heritage Consultant commission with a maximum available budget of £8,000 excluding VAT. The fee must include all professional time, research, meetings, travel, expenses and preparation of the required deliverables.
The tender is expected to be awarded and mobilised in late September 2026. The consultant must programme the work to support the wider feasibility project and the development of the RIBA Stage 2 proposals. All final outputs, approvals and contributions to the Phase 1 evaluation must be completed no later than 31 August 2027.

awardCriteria.description:
Tenders will be evaluated on the basis of the most advantageous tender, taking account of quality, relevant experience and value for money. The Council is not obliged to accept the lowest-priced tender.
1. Quality and clarity of proposed methodology: 25%
The suitability, robustness and clarity of the proposed approach to archival research, heritage assessment, significance analysis, stakeholder liaison, report preparation, quality assurance and delivery of the required outputs.
2. Relevant heritage expertise: 20%
The qualifications, knowledge and experience of the proposed consultant or team, including expertise in heritage significance assessment, conservation methodology, archival research and the history of leisure, lidos, coastal or marine heritage sites.
3. Price and value for money: 20%
The total fee, clarity of the fee breakdown, allocation of resources, any assumptions or exclusions and the extent to which the proposal provides value for money within the available budget.
4. Experience of comparable projects: 15%
Evidence of successfully completing similar heritage assessments, particularly for coastal, marine, outdoor leisure, historic building or National Lottery Heritage Fund supported projects.
5. Understanding of the brief and project context: 10%
The tenderer's understanding of the Lymington Sea Water Baths, the purpose of the commission and the relationship between heritage research, design development, community engagement, interpretation and future funding applications.
6. Ability to meet the programme and collaborate effectively: 10%
The tenderer's availability, capacity and proposed programme, together with their ability to work collaboratively with the Council, Project Manager, Design Team, Consultation and Engagement Consultant, museums, archives and other project partners.

lots.description:
Accountant in Bankruptcy (AiB) is an Executive Agency of the Scottish Government responsible for administering Scotland's statutory debt solutions. These include bankruptcy, Protected Trust Deeds and the Debt Arrangement Scheme.
To support the delivery of its statutory functions, AiB intends to establish a single-provider Framework Agreement for the provision of Insolvency Services across Scotland. The appointed provider will deliver insolvency administration services for bankruptcy cases where AiB has been appointed Trustee under the Bankruptcy (Scotland) Act 2016. The provider will administer allocated cases on AiB's behalf, while AiB will remain the appointed Trustee throughout.
The appointed provider will be expected to carry out the administration of cases in accordance with the Bankruptcy (Scotland) Act 2016 and any associated legislation, statutory guidance and operational instructions issued by AiB. An Operating Manual detailing the required bankruptcy administration processes will be provided to the successful provider.
The Services are expected to be required primarily throughout Scotland. However, occasions may arise where service delivery is required elsewhere within the United Kingdom and, exceptionally, overseas. Tenderers must demonstrate that they possess the capability, capacity and operational infrastructure necessary to deliver the Services effectively and consistently, irrespective of geographical location.
Between July 2022 and May 2026, approximately 3,179 insolvency cases were instructed, comprising 1,973 Debtor Applications and 1,206 Creditor Petitions. Under the proposed arrangements, AiB intends to retain the majority of Debtor Applications, with only more complex cases being allocated to the appointed provider. Forthcoming legislative changes may also result in a further reduction in the volume of cases allocated. Bidders should note that insolvency services are demand-led and historic volumes are provided for information only and do not constitute any guarantee of future case volumes or throughput.
Complex cases may include cases that involve trading activity, self-employed debtors, deceased debtor estates, legal entities (including partnerships, trusts and incorporated bodies), Scottish Charitable Incorporated Organisations (SCIOs), foreign property ownership, property portfolio ownership, tenanted property ownership, land ownership or crofting. The expectation for these cases would be for full administration.
The Framework Agreement will be established for an initial period of two years with the option for AiB to extend for up to two further periods of twelve months each; subject to satisfactory performance and continued business need.
This procurement is being conducted using the Restricted Procedure. This Contract Notice relates to the Selection Stage only. Interested economic operators are required to complete and submit the Single Procurement Document (SPD Scotland) and any associated selection-stage information by the stated deadline.

tender.description:
The London Borough of Tower Hamlets requires an Integrated Community Equipment Service (ICES) to provide adults and children living at home with a range of community equipment that supports independence, prevents hospital admissions and facilitates timely hospital discharge. The service supports the Council and NHS partners in meeting statutory duties under health and social care legislation. Key outcomes include:
Supporting residents to remain living independently at home.
Reducing unplanned hospital admissions.
Facilitating hospital discharge and reducing length of stay.
Reducing reliance on residential care and paid care services.
Promoting safety, independence, quality of life and end of life care.

The original extreme urgency caused by the dissolution of NRS still exists and there would not be enough time to complete a tender of this complexity in the foreseeable future. Therefore, section 13 of Schedule 5 to the Procurement Act 2023 applies to the direct award to Enabled Living Healthcare
This direct award is justified under Schedule 5, Section 13 of the Procurement Act 2023 (Extreme and Unavoidable Urgency). Following the insolvency of NRS Healthcare on 1 August 2025, there is an urgent requirement to maintain continuity of a critical statutory community equipment service supporting vulnerable adults and children, independent living, hospital discharge and prevention of hospital admissions. There is insufficient time to undertake a competitive procurement without risking interruption to essential health and social care services.

tender.riskDetails:
The contract supports delivery of a critical statutory service for adults and children requiring community equipment to maintain independence and support safe discharge from hospital. Key risks to contract performance include supply chain disruption affecting equipment availability, failure to meet delivery and installation timescales, inadequate servicing and maintenance of equipment, workforce capacity pressures, data protection breaches, and business continuity issues. There is also a risk of increased demand leading to service pressures and delays in provision. Robust contract management, KPI monitoring, escalation procedures, business continuity arrangements, equipment stock controls, and regular performance reviews will be implemented to mitigate these risks.
The market has recently experienced significant disruption following the insolvency of the previous provider, creating a risk of reduced market capacity and supply resilience. The proposed provider has existing infrastructure, workforce and operational arrangements in place to support continuity of service delivery.
